subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

The one shared Scene builds everything from kit primitives (SceneLayer, Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, SymbolChip) and passes an entityId to each. subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Grouping: steps/index.ts maps all nine outline.json entries to the same Scene and the same groupKey 'making-a-presentation'. Stage.tsx's sceneKey() returns `${groupKey}:${sceneId(Scene)}`, so every step gets the same key on the single motion.div. React therefore updates the mounted Scene with the new payload instead of remounting it. A single shared groupKey is the correct grouping for this one continuously evolving scene. An entity present in consecutive steps therefore keeps the same layoutId and animates in place. Every entity id is consumed by a rendered element. groupKey keeps the scene mounted, and the layoutIds carry entity identity.

subcomponents.title: Maintains clear boundaries and scope discipline

criteria.rationale: The title clause is met, but the dead-contract clause is not. The guidance says shared constants must actually be used, and that a dead or misleading contract is scored under this criterion even when it is declared in shared scene-kit source. src/presentation-kit/constants.ts:7 declares `export const SETTLE_MS = 850`. I traced the import graph, and no file consumes it. - The demo reaches the kit only through the barrel: Talk.tsx:1 and steps/Scene.tsx:3-4 import from '../../presentation-kit' or '../../../presentation-kit'. The barrel (index.ts:1-3) re-exports only Presentation, types and primitives. It does not re-export constants. - Inside the kit, constants.ts is imported directly in three places. Stage.tsx:2 takes DESIGN_H, DESIGN_W, LAYOUT_T and STAGE_LAYOUT. useFitScale.ts:2 takes DESIGN_H, DESIGN_W and STAGE_LAYOUT. primitives.tsx:5 takes ENTER_T and LAYOUT_T. Presentation.tsx:1-8 imports only Stage, chrome, nav, useFitScale and types. - The only other direct importers are tests. tests/kit.test.tsx:7 takes ENTER_DELAY, ENTER_T and LAYOUT_T. tests/motion.test.tsx:9 takes LAYOUT_T and ENTER_DELAY. - No importer names SETTLE_MS, and constants.ts never uses it internally. EASE and ENTER_DELAY are used inside the file. - scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:7 hardcodes its own `settle = 850` instead of using the constant. That makes SETTLE_MS a misleading timing contract that no code applies. On the panel: Judges B and C are borne out. Judge A is right that the title is consumed: Talk.tsx:5 passes `title`, and Presentation.tsx:18 renders it as the `main` aria-label. Judge A is also right that the demo-local organization is clean. But Judge A never checked the shared-constant clause, so neither point settles it, and the unused SETTLE_MS export leaves that clause unmet.
evidence: src/presentation-kit/constants.ts:7 declares `export const SETTLE_MS = 850`. Lines 1-11 show that no other constant in the file uses it.
src/presentation-kit/index.ts:1-3 re-exports only Presentation, types and nodes/primitives, so the demo cannot reach SETTLE_MS through the barrel.
The demo imports kit code only through the barrel: Talk.tsx:1 and steps/Scene.tsx:3-4. steps/index.ts:1 imports only the Step type.
The kit files that import constants.ts take only other names: Stage.tsx:2, useFitScale.ts:2 and nodes/primitives.tsx:5. Presentation.tsx:1-8 does not import constants.
The tests that import constants.ts also take only other names: tests/kit.test.tsx:7 (ENTER_DELAY, ENTER_T, LAYOUT_T) and tests/motion.test.tsx:9 (LAYOUT_T, ENTER_DELAY).
scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:7 hardcodes `settle = 850` instead of using SETTLE_MS, so the exported constant misleadingly suggests a shared settle contract that nothing applies.
The title clause is satisfied: Talk.tsx:5 passes `title`, and Presentation.tsx:10-18 forwards it and renders `<main aria-label={title}>`.

criteria.rationale: Port allocation is dynamic: freePort() listens on port 0 and withPreview passes that port with --strictPort. Termination of every started process is not met. The browser tests (E2E-001, E2E-002 and INT-002) start the preview and Chromium indirectly. Each runs `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through the shared command() helper (tests/integration.test.mjs:11-20). When that helper times out, it calls child.kill('SIGTERM') on the npm child alone and rejects at once. It does not await the npm child's exit, does not signal a process group (spawn has no detached option and there is no negative-pid kill), and does not reach the preview the script started. That preview is spawned at scripts/browser.mjs:34 as a grandchild of npm (package.json:13-14 maps verify and inspect to `node scripts/...`). Its only termination is in withPreview's finally block (scripts/browser.mjs:54-69), which runs only while the node verify/inspect process keeps executing JavaScript. The complete quoted scripts/browser.mjs and scripts/verify.mjs install no process.on('SIGTERM') handler and forward no signals. So nothing in the delivered code ties the test's SIGTERM on the npm wrapper to the preview's termination. Meanwhile the test rejects and isolated() deletes the working directory (line 33). assertCleanup (lines 43-52) runs only after command() resolves, so it never covers the timeout path. This is the named failure: a test that kills only the npm wrapper and leaves the preview server running. Panel A (pass) relies on freePort and assertCleanup. Both are accurate, but they cover only runs that finish normally, not the timeout path where the test kills only the wrapper, so they do not settle the requirement. Panel B (pass) itself notes that the timeout path signals only the npm wrapper, then sets it aside as a failure path. The requirement has no exception for failure paths; it requires that every started process be terminated. The material bears out Panel C's reason, so I rule C's verdict.
evidence: tests/integration.test.mjs:16 — the timeout handler runs `child.kill('SIGTERM'); no(new Error(...))`. The child is the spawned `npm` process (line 13). Its exit is never awaited and no proces…

subcomponents.title: Verified candidate-produced testing evidence

criteria.rationale: The only verified exploration in the packet is the round-1 retest. It covers one seam: the fixed-canvas fit and centering of step 8 at 390×844, 320×568 and 1440×900, in browse and present modes. The log says the other behaviors were not re-run, and that choice was the candidate's: it says no broad repeat of round 0's skill/scaffold journeys, navigation matrix or failure matrix was run. The packet holds no round-0 observations for those behaviors. The ledger says scaffold and generated-route behaviors were exercised and the sample observed, but it records no actions or results. The environment did not prevent these runs. Nothing recorded shows keyboard, swipe or direct-jump navigation, boundary clamping, mode-toggle position preservation, morph/enter/exit sequencing or attribution. Nothing recorded shows scaffold target resolution or the verify/render failure paths either. Most of the specs' user-visible behavior is therefore unexercised by the verified record. The candidate disclosed this, but the omission was its own choice, so it counts against coverage in proportion.
evidence: Exploration log: "No other product seam changed in the diff, so no broad repeat of round 0's skill/scaffold journeys, navigation matrix, or failure matrix was run."
Exploration log: only step 8 was visually reviewed, and no other presentations or intermediate viewports were checked.
Ledger: the round-0 exercise of scaffold and generated-route behaviors is asserted, but no observations are recorded.
Screenshots 01, 05 and 09 are marked defective (missing capture metadata), so they cannot support any claim.
judging basis: consensus-fail

The unit log does show 66 tests passed. The ledger's statement that scaffold and generated-route behaviors were exercised in disposable projects also has no artifact.

subcomponents.title: Observable assumption handling

criteria.rationale: The record shows two reproduced deviations from the approved requirements: the A-001 canvas clipping at 390px, and the A-002 unreadable diagram text at narrow widths against AT-003's readability expectation. Both are surfaced as findings, and A-002 is also written up as a ledger decision with options (a)–(d). The ledger also raises the AT-003 departing-entity vs cumulative-sample conflict, the monorepo partial-anchor target question, the helper-versus-SKILL.md integration split, and the conversational-journey limitation. I found no observed deviation that the record leaves out.
evidence: The A-002 ledger entry cites the AT-003 readability expectation and the fixed-canvas requirement, and lists options (a)–(d).
The findings history records A-001 (clipped canvas) and A-002 (3–7 px text).
The ledger poses the AT-003 departing-entity question and the monorepo anchor question as explicit questions with options and consequences.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The ledger separates what the approved spec and test plan say from its own readings. It cites SKILL.md line ranges and the AT-001/AT-003 text, and it flags the monorepo kit+registry-without-build case as a judgement call. It states plainly that A-001 was a defect and fixed it. For A-002 it says the observed scaling follows the approved uniform-scale design. It still records A-002 as an open finding that leaves the AT-003 readability expectation unmet, so the reproduced behavior is not called acceptable or optional.
evidence: A-001 is called a defect and fixed, with the cause and the regression coverage stated.
A-002 is stated as unmet: 'the narrow-viewport readability expectation in AT-003 stays unmet for the dense steps.'
The ledger limits its own evidence claims, for example that I-23 evidence must not be described as proving a partial scaffold builds and routes.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The A-002 resolution would change approved requirements (the no-reflow rule, the canvas default, or AT-003's scope). The candidate did not take that decision itself. It made no tracked change, listed options with consequences, and escalated to the user. The A-001 defect sat within the approved definition, so fixing it directly was proportionate. The monorepo and helper readings were made within the existing spec text, with the remaining uncertainty noted and the pending user decisions stated.
evidence: The A-002 ruling says: 'Making it readable requires changing an approved requirement' and 'Choosing which one gives way is a change to approved scope, so it belongs to the user.'
A-001 was fixed with no change to the scale math, canvas size or styling, plus regression tests.
The monorepo ruling states 'No requirement is changed' and marks what would be a new requirement.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The handoff names the open decisions and limitations. It leads with A-002 (narrow-viewport text too small, with the 390px and 320px evidence) and points to the findings and the assumptions ledger. It lists the two unresolved decisions by subject: AT-003 departing entities versus the cumulative sample, and the monorepo root with kit and registry but no build anchor. It carries the conversational-journey limitation, the unrun suites and CI, the AXI stall and the risky implementation assumptions. It does not repeat the A-002 options (a)-(d) and frames the fix as preserving fixed-canvas behavior, which is weaker than the ledger. A-002 is named with its subject and the ledger is referenced, so the decision is preserved.
evidence: The Decision brief names A-002 and tells the reviewer to review it first.
The "Unresolved decision count: 2" list names both decisions with options and consequences.
The handoff carries the conversation limitation, the not-exercised list, and the CI/validation disclaimers.
judging basis: majority-pass

votes.rationale: Talk.tsx renders the kit's Presentation with STEPS, title and initialMode. It does not reimplement navigation, stage or chrome. steps/index.ts builds typed kit Step objects. The one shared Scene builds everything from kit primitives (SceneLayer, Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, SymbolChip) and passes an entityId to each. The kit's Node turns that into layoutId and layout on a motion.div, so the demo uses the kit's morph mechanism instead of duplicating it. AnimatePresence in Scene handles conditional entry and exit.

steps/Scene.tsx: imports Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, SymbolChip, SceneLayer and SceneProps from presentation-kit; every node gets entityId={entity(...)}
presentation-kit/nodes/primitives.tsx Node: motion.div with layout, layoutId={entityId}, data-presentation-entity
presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx: wires usePresentationNav, Stage, Header, Footer and Toc

votes.rationale: The Talk and the shared Scene use the kit's public API. They don't bypass it or rebuild its mechanisms. Scene.tsx composes SceneLayer, Box, Label, Arrow, Frame and SymbolChip from the kit barrel. Each node gets an entityId, and the kit's Node turns that into motion layout/layoutId. The demo has no navigation, fit-scale or transition code of its own. The kit's Stage supplies LayoutGroup, AnimatePresence and the mount keying.

result.rationale: Port allocation is dynamic: freePort() listens on port 0 and withPreview passes that port with --strictPort. Termination of every started process is not met. The browser tests (E2E-001, E2E-002 and INT-002) start the preview and Chromium indirectly. Each runs `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through the shared command() helper (tests/integration.test.mjs:11-20). When that helper times out, it calls child.kill('SIGTERM') on the npm child alone and rejects at once. It does not await the npm child's exit, does not signal a process group (spawn has no detached option and there is no negative-pid kill), and does not reach the preview the script started. That preview is spawned at scripts/browser.mjs:34 as a grandchild of npm (package.json:13-14 maps verify and inspect to `node scripts/...`). Its only termination is in withPreview's finally block (scripts/browser.mjs:54-69), which runs only while the node verify/inspect process keeps executing JavaScript. The complete quoted scripts/browser.mjs and scripts/verify.mjs install no process.on('SIGTERM') handler and forward no signals. So nothing in the delivered code ties the test's SIGTERM on the npm wrapper to the preview's termination. Meanwhile the test rejects and isolated() deletes the working directory (line 33). assertCleanup (lines 43-52) runs only after command() resolves, so it never covers the timeout path. This is the named failure: a test that kills only the npm wrapper and leaves the preview server running. Panel A (pass) relies on freePort and assertCleanup. Both are accurate, but they cover only runs that finish normally, not the timeout path where the test kills only the wrapper, so they do not settle the requirement. Panel B (pass) itself notes that the timeout path signals only the npm wrapper, then sets it aside as a failure path. The requirement has no exception for failure paths; it requires that every started process be terminated. The material bears out Panel C's reason, so I rule C's verdict.

first_results.rationale: Ports are allocated dynamically: freePort() calls listen(0) and the preview runs with --strictPort. But the criterion also requires the tests to terminate every process they start, and it names the failure case: a test that kills only the npm wrapper and leaves the preview running. The shared command() helper in tests/integration.test.mjs spawns `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect`. Its timeout handler only calls child.kill('SIGTERM') on that npm child and rejects at once. It does not kill descendants and does not wait for them to exit. The preview server is a grandchild: node scripts/verify.mjs or scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs (package.json) calls withPreview, which spawns vite preview. Its only cleanup is a finally block in withPreview. Neither scripts/browser.mjs nor scripts/verify.mjs installs a SIGTERM handler, so a signal that ends the script process skips that finally block and leaves the vite preview running. assertCleanup() only runs after command() resolves, so the rejected timeout path gets no cleanup check. Judge C's reason is borne out and decides the requirement, so I rule C's fail. Judges A and B both passed after checking only the successful path: dynamic ports, plus assertCleanup confirming the preview and browser PIDs had exited. That evidence does not cover the timeout path, where only the npm wrapper is killed. Judge B even noted that the timeout path signals only the npm wrapper, then set it aside as a failure path. The criterion names exactly that scenario, so neither pass reason decides the requirement.

audit_results.rationale: The claim is a counterexample fail. It must show from the quoted lines that a test 'kills only an npm or npx wrapper and leaves the preview server running.' The quoted tests/integration.test.mjs:16 does show the first half: on timeout, command() sends SIGTERM only to the spawned npm child and rejects without waiting. The quoted lines do not show the second half, that the preview survives. That depends on what happens to the SIGTERM after npm receives it. Does npm or its shell forward the signal to node scripts/verify.mjs? Does that script, or any module it loads, install a SIGTERM handler that lets withPreview's finally block run? The claim says neither scripts/browser.mjs nor scripts/verify.mjs installs a SIGTERM handler. But only scripts/browser.mjs:31-69 and scripts/verify.mjs:5-8 are quoted, not the whole files, and nothing quoted covers npm's signal handling. So the absence of a handler, and the orphaned preview it would cause, comes from unquoted code and assumed runtime behaviour, not from the cited lines. The quoted material supports the rest: dynamic ports (freePort, --strictPort) and a finally-based cleanup that awaits the preview's exit on every path inside the script. It neither proves nor disproves that the preview is left running after a timeout. No truncation or omission marker applies, so this is the burden of the judge under audit: insufficient.

engineering-quality.rationale: The auditor accepts that ports are dynamic and that assertCleanup verifies the preview and browser PIDs exited. Their only argument is the timeout branch of command(), which sends SIGTERM to the spawned npm process. That branch runs only if a script hangs for the full 180 s, and nothing in the material shows that happening. In those runs the tests don't start the preview themselves. The npm script starts it through withPreview as a direct child (process.execPath running vite.js, not an npx wrapper), and that script's nested finally blocks send SIGTERM and then SIGKILL and wait for the exit. After every run, the tests check through assertCleanup that each logged preview and browser PID is reported as cleaned and no longer exists. INT-003, the one test that starts a preview itself, calls withPreview directly and closes it in finally. The claim that a timeout leaves the server running relies on unshown behavior: the verify script's signal handling isn't in the material, and npm normally passes SIGTERM on to the script it runs. So the material doesn't establish the guidance's fail case of a test that kills only the wrapper and leaves the preview server running, and the pass stands.
